name: Physical Therapy Clinics
h1: AI Phone Agent for Physical Therapy Clinics: Referral Intake
metaDescription: Calldesk answers physical therapy clinic calls: referral intake, evaluation scheduling, authorization questions and cancellations from patients in plans.
intro: A physical therapy clinic fills its week with courses of treatment: a patient comes two or three times a week for several weeks, so the schedule is a lattice of recurring slots. Every cancellation leaves a gap, and every missed call from a new referral risks losing the evaluation to another clinic. Many new patients arrive with a referral from a surgeon or primary care doctor, often after a procedure, and they call to schedule at the surgeon's suggestion within a particular window. Others are walk-in style callers with an athletic injury who want to know how soon they can be seen and whether insurance requires a referral. Therapists are working one-on-one with patients and cannot answer, and the front desk may be shared with the clinic's billing. The calls also include insurance authorization questions, referral paperwork follow-ups from doctors' offices, and patients checking what to wear and how long the first visit lasts. A Calldesk agent can answer as the clinic's AI assistant, gather referral and insurance details, offer an evaluation slot on a connected calendar, handle cancellations, and route clinical questions to a therapist. It does not give exercise or medical advice. Batch calls can contact patients who stopped attending mid-plan.
callTypes: Post-surgery patients scheduling an initial evaluation within a doctor's window
Self-referred callers with a sports or work injury asking how soon they can start
Physician offices calling about referral paperwork or a patient's start date
Patients rescheduling or cancelling a visit in an ongoing plan
Insurance questions about visit limits, copays and authorization
Outbound check-ins with patients who stopped attending before finishing a plan

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks for calling the clinic. I'm the clinic's AI assistant. Are you booking a first visit or changing an existing appointment?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: First visit. My surgeon wants me in PT within two weeks of my knee replacement.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks. May I have your name, and the surgeon's name or office that referred you?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Harold Pruitt, referred by Dr. Anand at the orthopedic group.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks, Harold. When was your surgery, and do you already have the written referral?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Surgery was Monday. The referral is coming from their office.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I'll note that. The first evaluation takes about an hour. We have Monday at 8:30 or Tuesday at 1:15 open, which should fit your two-week window. Which one suits you?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Booked. Please bring your insurance card and any discharge papers, and wear loose clothing. The clinic will check your insurance and the referral before the visit.

setupSteps: Create an agent from the appointment-booking template and list evaluation, follow-up and specialty visit types with their lengths.
Connect a calendar with evaluation slots, and add a path for rescheduling that preserves the patient's name and plan.
Write extraction fields for referring provider, surgery or injury date, insurance and whether a written referral is in hand.
Add the knowledge base: referral rules as the clinic states them, what to bring, parking, and visit length.
Add a transfer to a therapist or front desk for clinical questions, test the flows, publish, and plan any outbound follow-ups.

featuresUsed.howItHelps: Books initial evaluations within the physician's recommended window and refills slots when patients cancel.
Records referring doctor, surgery date, insurance and referral status for the intake coordinator.
Answers parking, what-to-bring and visit-length questions without a staff member picking up.
Moves clinical questions and physician-office calls to a therapist or coordinator.
Gives the front desk a short note on each call, so cancellations and new referrals can be acted on quickly.

considerations: Patient information may be protected health information. Calldesk makes no HIPAA certification claim, so your compliance advisor or counsel should decide whether and how a voice agent fits your obligations.
The agent should not give exercise advice, pain management guidance or opinions on recovery. Route those questions to a therapist.
Insurance and referral requirements vary by payer and state. The agent states the clinic's published guidance and does not promise coverage.
Outbound follow-ups to patients who stopped attending are calls requiring consent; check with your own counsel, including TCPA rules.

faq.q: Does the agent verify referrals or insurance?
faq.a: No. It collects the details and records whether paperwork is in hand. Verification stays with the clinic's coordinator.
Yes. A path can recognize a call from a doctor's office, take the patient's name and referral details, and transfer to the coordinator.

faq.q: How does it handle a patient in pain?
faq.a: The agent does not give medical advice. If a caller describes severe symptoms, the flow can advise emergency care and transfer to staff according to wording your clinicians approve.

faq.q: Can it schedule a whole course of visits?
faq.a: It books individual slots on the calendar. A full series is usually set by the therapist at the evaluation, or by a flow you design to book several visits.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Pricing is per talk-minute, from 2 cents on Lite to 9 cents on Pro, plus carrier charges. The pricing page lists current tiers.
